### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d558de0ae0ef161e5567da4dde1470feca745fe7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8ed8877a65dd5af0b0c399aad7301929ecd73818` — the merge of head `8239d579561ba2995d9b3775da4c17bc13a05f43` into base `d558de0ae0ef161e5567da4dde1470feca745fe7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8ed8877a65dd5af0b0c399aad7301929ecd73818 && git checkout 8ed8877a65dd5af0b0c399aad7301929ecd73818
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d558de0ae0ef161e5567da4dde1470feca745fe7 8239d579561ba2995d9b3775da4c17bc13a05f43 && git checkout -B drift-repro d558de0ae0ef161e5567da4dde1470feca745fe7 && git merge --no-ff 8239d579561ba2995d9b3775da4c17bc13a05f43

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d558de0ae0ef161e5567da4dde1470feca745fe7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fb54ecbac2ece9db0158af547848bf42a9a8e002`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts + packages/spec/liveness/object.json (the ledger is no face hit: on this file list the face reader returns the schema file alone, the schema face; it is widened in as the one in-diff file that attests the key's readers)
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Read: card #36819 (body and all seven comments), PR #37302 (body, file list of four, net diff of head `fb54ecb` against `main`), and the 74 check-runs on the head. The cited code was read on `origin/main` `80da086`; `rowActionArrangement.ts`, `components/RowActionMenu.tsx`, `components/RowContextMenu.tsx`, `components/SelectionBar.tsx` and `types/src/ui-action.ts` are unchanged between the PR's merge-base `4fb03eb` and that commit, and the lines read in `ObjectGrid.tsx` and `objectGridActionsColumn.tsx` did not move in meaning.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged. Right.** The schema file changes in two hunks, the module docblock's `record` bullet and the `record` arm's `.describe()` string. No shape, pattern, limit, refinement, alias or export moves; `api-surface` and the authorable surface carry no diff and their gates are green.
- **Published text: one description, on two schemas. Right.** `OBJECT_ACTION_LAYOUT_SCHEMA` is the one leaf `ObjectSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` share, so the new string reaches both. The two regenerated rows (`content/docs/references/data/object.mdx:206` and `:743`) equal it. On `main` no other generated file carries the old string, so nothing is left stale.
- **Ledger: text and a date on two rows. Right.** `actionLayout` and `actionLayout.record` change `evidence`, `note` (the child) and `verifiedAt` (2026-11-23 to 2026-11-25); no `status` moves and no row is added or dropped. Dropping "the ONE reader" is right: `main` has a second reader. Both new anchors resolve on `main` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:941` `ObjectGrid`, `RowActionMenu.tsx:320` `planRowActionMenu`) and `Spec property liveness` is green. The ledger ships in the tarball (`files` lists `liveness`), so this is published text too.
- **Behaviour: none changed by this diff.** The row-menu ordering landed with PR #36815; this PR only describes it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start in both the PR body and the changeset. Right on all three: nothing an author can write is added, refused or given a new meaning here (the meaning moved in the behaviour PR), `none` takes `patch`, and no arm is owed. Both `Check Changeset` runs are green. The changeset body repeats the sentence S1 is about; it ships as `CHANGELOG.md` text, so the S1 round should carry it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both dev reports (7164928676, 7165886072). Nothing to answer.
- Round-1 out-of-scope note (the ledger named `arrangedHeaderActions` "the ONE reader"): answered by the claim amendment (7165739373) and fixed on this head.
- Round-2 flag (the dev left the PR body for the seat to write): closed. The body read at this head carries the ledger bullet and both declaration lines.
- Declared local narrowing (16 of 104 gate families run locally): answered by the head's check-runs. 74 runs, all completed: 62 success, 12 skipped, none red, none pending. `Lint UI` is among the skipped (no `ui/` path in the diff); the other ten required contexts are success.
- File surface: the four changed files sit inside the claim plus its amendment. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join. No finding.
- For the seat, outside the diff (read, not reviewed): `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx:406-408` on `main` carries the same two-surface sentence and the same button sentence as S1. It needs a carrier of its own or a place in S1's round; that is the seat's call.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts`**, judged against ADR-0085's note of 2026-11-23 ("The `record` arm orders every surface that draws a record's actions") and the first consumer on `main`. Each sentence the diff adds, tried against the code:

- "orders a grid row's ⋮ menu": holds. `ObjectGrid.tsx:1419-1420` reads `objectSchema.actionLayout.record` and ranks the row defs (`rankRowActionDefs`); `objectGridActionsColumn.tsx:175` hands those defs to the cell (`:260`), whose plan orders the menu-bound ones (`RowActionMenu.tsx:370`, `orderRowMenuActions`). The rank rides the def object, and every filter between the two keeps object identity.
- "and its right-click menu": holds. `ObjectGrid.tsx:3794` gives `RowContextMenuItems` the same `rowActionMenuProps(row)`, so the same ranked defs, and it plans with an inline budget of 0 (`RowContextMenu.tsx:98`). A selection of two or more opens the bulk menu, which does not read the arm; the text says the row's menu, so it stands.
- "the actions `pinned` names first, then those `more` names, then the rest as before": holds. The rank is `pinned` then `more`, first occurrence (`rowActionArrangement.ts:50-52`); ranked defs sort by rank and the rest keep their incoming order (`:72-78`), which is overflow primaries above secondaries as before. Pinned by `rowContextMenu-28434.test.tsx:423-439`.
- "which action a row draws as its button does not change": holds for the row's own button. `inline` is cut from the surviving primaries in declared order (`RowActionMenu.tsx:365-367`) before `orderRowMenuActions` runs, and `rankRowActionDefs` keeps the defs' order. Pinned at `rowContextMenu-28434.test.tsx:430`.
- "Omit to draw each as before": holds. No arm answers the defs by reference (`rowActionArrangement.ts:48`); an object with only a `list` arm lists as before (`rowContextMenu-28434.test.tsx:441-452`). The docblock's "The `list` arm has one reader today" still holds: the grid reads `record` alone.

No must-fix.

S1 (should-fix) — the text names two of the three row surfaces the order reaches, and the third is the one where buttons do move.
On a list page a row draws no "⋮" cell at all (`drawRowControls: !listPageGrid`, `ObjectGrid.tsx:2464`). One selected record's actions are drawn there by the selection bar, from the same props and the same ranked defs (`singleRowMenu`, `ObjectGrid.tsx:3816`; `SelectionBar.tsx:158`, `useRowActionPlan(menu, 0)`). The bar lists the plan's order (`singleRecordEntries`) and draws its first three as labelled buttons (`planExposedEntries`, `SELECTION_EXPOSED_ACTIONS = 3`). So with more than three actions on offer, `actionLayout.record` decides which of the record's actions are the bar's buttons. `rowActionArrangement.ts:27-31` names this surface itself: "the cell, the context menu, the selection bar's one-record menu". The describe does not name it, and the sentence standing nearest says the button does not change. An author, or an AI writing metadata from the describe, predicts the list page wrongly, which is the card's own defect on one more surface. To fix: name the list page selection bar's one-record actions among the surfaces the order leads, and scope the button sentence to the row's own inline button (or say the bar's buttons are the first of that order). Carry it to the docblock bullet, the two regenerated rows and the changeset sentence.

N1 (nit) — "leads" and "first" are true of the object's actions, not of the menu's top slot. The "⋮" menu lists its built-in Edit above them and Delete last (`RowActionMenu.tsx`, `RowActionMenuItems`), and the right-click menu lists its cell items and Open above them. The sibling `pinned` description ("New, Edit and Delete keep their fixed places") covers it for a reader who joins the two.

N2 (nit) — the row menus list only actions also placed at `list_item` (`objectViewListRenderer.tsx`, `rowActionDefs`), so the arm reorders what a row already offers and adds nothing to it. A row-only action cannot be named in the arm (`object-action-layout-not-placed`, `packages/lint/src/validate-object-action-layout.ts`). "orders" and "the rest as before" say this well enough; one clause would say it outright.

**`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`** (in the diff, attests the contract). The two rows agree with the code: the grid reads the arm and ranks (`ObjectGrid.tsx:1419-1420`), `planRowActionMenu` orders with `orderRowMenuActions`, the header reader is described as before, and the row's inline button is unchanged. The `planRowActionMenu` anchor is the one funnel all three row surfaces pass through, so the pointer itself is whole; the words beside it name two surfaces. S1's round should add the selection bar there as well.

N3 (nit) — the grandchild rows `actionLayout.record.pinned` and `.more` still name the record header alone and keep `verifiedAt` 2026-11-23. Both remain true as far as they go.

S1 is open on this head: its fix earns a delta review. The nits need no round.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2d3d65761a6bb2fc73e402a6aa397e837338eae5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts + packages/spec/liveness/object.json, content/docs/ui/actions.mdx (neither is a face hit: on this file list the face reader returns the schema file alone; the ledger is widened in as the in-diff file that attests the key's readers, the guide paragraph because this round moved it for S1)
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta review (record 7178489745: PASS on `fb54ecb`, should-fix S1 open, nits N1 to N3). Read: the two card comments added since (7178504889, 7178678768), the PR body and its file list of five, the delta `fb54ecb..2d3d657` (two commits, five files) and the check-runs on the new head. Only what moved is judged. The cited code was read on `origin/main` `02520ab`; `ui/packages/plugin-grid` and `ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` are unchanged since the `80da086` the first record read.

S1: closed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: still unchanged. Right.** The delta in the schema file is the docblock's `record` bullet and the `record` arm's `.describe()` string again; no shape, pattern, limit, refinement or export moves.
- **Published text. Right.** The new describe string (576 characters) is carried whole by both regenerated rows (`content/docs/references/data/object.mdx:206` and `:743`).
- **Ledger. Right.** The same two rows change `evidence`, `note` and `verifiedAt` (now 2026-11-26, not in the future); no `status` moves. The new anchor `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/components/SelectionBar.tsx#planExposedEntries` exists on `main` (`SelectionBar.tsx:73`, exported) and `Spec property liveness` is green on this head.
- **Guide page.** `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` changes one paragraph of prose, inside the claim as amended (7178504889).

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `@objectstack/spec` `patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start in the PR body and the changeset. The changeset's sentence now says what the describe says, the selection bar included, and names the guide page and the ledger.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the round-3 report (7178678768). Nothing to answer.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-26 00:24 UTC: 71 runs, 25 success, 12 skipped, 34 still in progress, none red. Green so far: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, one `Check Changeset`. Still running: `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, the second `Check Changeset`, `Test Core` shards 1 to 10 and `Test UI` shards 1 to 16. The `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and `Test UI` contexts had not reported yet. This record judges the text; it says nothing for a run that has not concluded, and the seat reads them all green before it queues.
- The PR body at this head carries the round-3 text, with three lines for the seat to correct (prose, no effect on this record): the Acceptance note still says `actions.mdx` is untouched; the two-minute check greps `grid row's ⋮ menu` and expects 2, and that string is no longer in `object.mdx` (0 at this head; `the row's ⋮ menu` gives 2); and the selection-bar lines `ObjectGrid.tsx:2447` and `:3799` are the PR tree's, not `02520ab`'s, where the same code sits at `:2464` and `:3816`. The round-3 dev report carries the same two line numbers.
- File surface: the five changed files sit inside the claim and its two amendments. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no join in the delta. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts`**: each sentence the delta adds, tried against `main`.

- "on a list page, the selection bar's actions for one selected record": holds. The bar is handed one record's row menu only on a list page with exactly one row selected (`ObjectGrid.tsx:3816`), where rows draw no control of their own (`:2464`). It plans from the same ranked defs with an inline budget of 0 (`SelectionBar.tsx:158`), so every surviving action passes through `orderRowMenuActions`, and `singleRecordEntries` (`:57`) lists them in that order ahead of the built-ins.
- "`pinned` names first, then `more` names, then the rest as before": holds there as on the two menus, for the same reason (`rowActionArrangement.ts:50-52`, `:72-78`).
- "The selection bar's buttons, at most three, are the first of that order": holds. `planExposedEntries` (`SelectionBar.tsx:73-83`) takes the first `SELECTION_EXPOSED_ACTIONS = 3` (`:43`) entries it admits, in order, and the width fit only trims from the end (`:80`), so the actions drawn as buttons are always a prefix of the order.
- "a row's own inline button does not change": holds, as judged on the previous head (`RowActionMenu.tsx:365-367`), and it is now scoped to the surface it is true of.
- "the actions a grid row already offers, adding none": holds, and takes N2. The row's defs are the object's actions placed at `list_item`; the arm ranks the ones it names and supplies none.

The docblock bullet says the same in the same order. With the third surface named and the button sentence scoped, S1 is fixed in the schema file, the two regenerated rows and the changeset.

**`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`**: the two rows agree with the code. `planRowActionMenu` is the funnel all three row surfaces pass through, the parentheses beside it now name all three, and `planExposedEntries` is where the bar's buttons are chosen.

**`content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`**: the `record` paragraph now carries the same three statements, and each holds as above.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N4 (nit) — the button sentence leans on the clause before it for "one selected record". With two or more rows selected the bar draws the view's bulk actions, which the arm does not order; and with fewer than three actions on offer the built-in Edit, and Delete, take button slots too. Neither changes which actions the arm puts first.

N5 (nit) — the ledger says the bar draws "the first three of that order" where the describe says "at most three"; the bar's width can leave fewer.

N1 and N3 from the earlier record stand as nits, untouched by this round: built-in Edit sits above the named actions in the "⋮" menu, and the grandchild rows `actionLayout.record.pinned` and `.more` still name the header alone.

Nothing above a nit is open on this head, so this round ends the review of the text.
